mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs for corporate expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.05% over the prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year CPI increase exceeding 2.5% indicates accelerating inflation that triggers Federal Reserve rate hikes within 30 days, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in nonfarm payrolls signals labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through a demand expansion channel.
evidence_refs: fact:June 2017 UNRATE at 8.5% and PAYEMS at 131,900.0 (up 100k from prior month)
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases by at least 100k, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 650,000 units per month indicates weak residential investment that reduces GDP growth momentum, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as housing contributes 15% to GDP and signals broader consumer weakness.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST falls below 650.0, or Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 95.0 for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as manufacturing accounts for 12% of GDP.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 95.0 for two months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate above 8.0% indicates persistent labor market slack that suppresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer demand accounts for 70% of GDP.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%, or Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales below 400,000 million dollars signals weak consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending drives 70% of GDP.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS falls below 400,000, or Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Federal Funds rate above 1.0% during a monetary tightening cycle indicates aggressive rate hikes that increase equity discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as bond yields rise and risk appetite declines.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.0% during a tightening cycle, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
